claims.text: Surface compositional heterogeneity is the primary governing factor for premelting and melting behavior in HEA nanoparticles.
Low-cohesive-energy elements become enriched at the nanoparticle surface.
Surface enrichment of low-cohesive-energy elements reduces local surface energy and cohesive forces.
Reduced local surface energy and cohesive forces lower the activation barrier for surface diffusion and liquid-phase nucleation.
The baseline particles are equiatomic, approximately 5–10 nm HEA nanoparticles with a random and uniform elemental distribution in both bulk and surface regions.
Mild vacuum annealing can induce controlled surface segregation of a selected low-cohesive-energy element while otherwise retaining a matched nanoparticle system.
Ni is an example of a suitable low-cohesive-energy element for the proposed segregation experiment.
The relevant structural mediator is the degree of surface enrichment, measurable as a surface-to-bulk concentration ratio.
Surface enrichment of low-cohesive-energy atoms causes surface atom mobility to begin at a lower temperature.
Surface enrichment of low-cohesive-energy atoms lowers the overall melting temperature.
Surface-segregated particles will exhibit premelting onset temperatures approximately 20–50 K below those of uniform particles.
Surface-segregated particles will exhibit overall melting temperatures approximately 20–50 K below those of uniform particles.
The melting and premelting effects of surface segregation will diminish for particle diameters greater than 15 nm.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to equiatomic HEA nanoparticles with diameters from 3 to 20 nm.
The hypothesis is expected to apply when differences in cohesive energy among the constituent elements do not exceed approximately 20%.
The magnitude of the temperature shift depends on the degree of segregation and the cohesive-energy contrast among elements.
A difference of less than 5 K between matched segregated and uniform particles would count as no meaningful change within experimental uncertainty.
